title: ClockClear
question: How does a wall clock work?
hook: A falling weight, a train of gears, and a pendulum that lets them move one tooth per swing. Take a clock apart in 3D, follow the escapement tick by tick, and see why a hot day makes it lose ten seconds.

explainer.title: A clock counts swings
explainer.text: A pendulum clock has five parts in a row: a weight or spring for power, a train of gears, an escapement, a pendulum and the hands. It does not measure time directly. It counts the pendulum's swings, 3,600 of them an hour in this clock.

explainer.title: The pendulum keeps the beat
explainer.text: A pendulum's period is 2π times the square root of its length over gravity. Its mass does not matter, and a small swing hardly does. A pendulum 99.4 cm long takes one second per swing. Heat makes the rod longer and the clock slower, so it is tuned with a nut under the bob.

explainer.title: The escapement: lock, push, drop
explainer.text: The anchor rocks with the pendulum and catches the escape wheel's teeth on two pallets. On each swing one tooth is released, slides down a slanted face to give the pendulum a small push, and drops until the other pallet catches the next tooth. That landing is the tick.

explainer.title: Gears do the arithmetic
explainer.text: Wheels of 96, 60 and 56 teeth drive pinions of 8, 8 and 7. The ratios 12, 7.5 and 8 multiply to 720, so the escape wheel turns once a minute while the drum turns once in twelve hours. Sixteen turns of line run the clock for eight days on about 58 joules.

explainer.title: Two hands, one centre, and a bell
explainer.text: Behind the dial, four wheels (36, 36, 6 and 72 teeth) turn the hour hand exactly 12 times slower than the minute hand around the same centre. For striking, a rack falls onto a stepped cam called the snail, and the depth of the step sets how many blows the hammer gives.

explainer.title: The clock on your wall
explainer.text: Most wall clocks now replace the pendulum with a quartz crystal vibrating 32,768 times a second. A chip halves that fifteen times to one pulse a second, and each pulse flips a tiny motor half a turn. No two crystals match exactly, so clocks drift apart by seconds a week.

concepts.def: A weight on a rod that swings at a steady rate set by its length and by gravity.
The time for one full swing there and back: 2π√(L/g). A 99.4 cm pendulum has a period of 2 seconds.
The mechanism that releases the gear train one tooth per swing and gives the pendulum a small push each time.
One of the two hard faces on the anchor that catch and release the escape wheel's teeth.
An escapement whose locking faces are curved around the anchor's pivot, so the wheel stands still instead of being pushed backwards.
The gears that carry power from the weight or spring to the escape wheel, speeding up at each step.
Teeth on the driving wheel divided by teeth on the pinion it drives: how many times faster the pinion turns.
The four wheels behind the dial that turn the hour hand 12 times slower than the minute hand.
A battery clock mechanism timed by a quartz crystal, with a small stepper motor turning the hands.
